deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics: no formulas, derivations or computations. It is a pencil draft, with deletions, of a methodological introduction to natural philosophy. It is a reworked version of material on the previous folio, which numbers the corresponding statement III; here it is numbered II.

The argument, step by step:
(1) Question II: from what is the connection of things (Zusammenhang der Dinge) to be found?
(2) Answer, in quotation marks: from the connection of appearances (Zusammenhang der Erscheinungen).
(3) Deliberate reflection on nature finds already given a representation of sense-things in definite spatial and temporal relations.
(4) As is well known, the qualities of the marks of sense-things are taken solely from our sensation and do not exist outside us. The examples listed are colours, sound, tone, smell, taste, warmth or cold. This is the standard Lockean/Helmholtzian primary/secondary-quality distinction.
(5) Hence what the connection of things must be known from are quantitative relations. These are the spatial and temporal relations of sense-things and the intensity relations of their marks, together with the (degrees of) their qualitative differences.
(6) Knowledge of the connection of things must come from reflecting on the observed connection of these magnitude relations (Größenverhältnisse). The previous page adds that the general laws of nature are to be found in this way.

In modern terms this is a programmatic statement. Physical explanation is to be built only on measurable quantities (space-time relations and intensities), and its laws are to be inferred from observed functional dependencies among them. It is a methodological prelude to Riemann's field-theoretic natural philosophy; no mathematical problem is being solved.
errors: No mathematical content, so no errors to check. Philosophically, the claim that qualitative differences are reducible to quantitative relations is asserted rather than argued; this is a draft.

results.what: Methodological principle: the connection of things is to be inferred from the connection of appearances, i.e. from quantitative space-time and intensity relations. Secondary qualities are subjective.
results.modern_name: Primary/secondary quality distinction; quantitative (measurement-based) foundation of physical explanation
results.usually_credited_to: Galileo, Locke (secondary qualities); in 19th-c. German physiology J. Müller and Helmholtz; Herbart for the psychological framing

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of Riemann's known natural-philosophical/epistemological fragments; similar statements appear in the Naturphilosophie pieces printed in the Gesammelte Werke. The ideas were commonplace in his time, and there is no mathematical content.
transcription_corrections: 'Raumdingen'/'Raumdinge' should read 'Sinnendingen'/'Sinnendinge' throughout, consistent with the previous page and the handwriting.
Line 3 reads 'Aus dem Zusammenhange der Erscheinungen.' — correct as given.
'gegeben {+ist+}': 'gegeben' is underlined, and 'ist' follows on the line rather than being an insertion.

'Die Qualität / Es ist jedoch bekanntlich die Qualität' is better read as one line: 'Es ist jedoch bekanntlich die Qualität' with 'Qualität' underlined. The first fragment appears to be a deletion or overwrite.
'Dinge {+erklärt[?]+} [-gefunden-]' is better read as 'erkannt' written over/above deleted 'gefunden', matching the previous page's 'erkannt werden muß'.
'Intensitätsverhältnisse der Materie[?] [?] und ihre Qualitätsunterschiede[?]' is likely 'die Intensitätsverhältnisse der Merkmale und ihre Qualitätsunterschiede', compare the previous page.

'Aus dem Nachdenken über den Causalzusammenhang Zusammenhang' is likely 'Aus dem Nachdenken über den beobachteten Zusammenhang dieser Größenverhältnisse muss sich die Erkenntniss des Zusammenhangs der Dinge ergeben', compare the previous page's 'beobachteten Zusammenhang dieser Größenverhältnisse'.
